summary: This benchmark evaluates a patch-repetition viewpoint selection heuristic against directional baselines and an empirical hindsight oracle across DTU scenes 1 and 6. The study demonstrates that the heuristic failed to achieve its targeted 5 percentage point accuracy improvement primarily because total available selection headroom was bounded at +1.27 and +0.37 percentage points under the tested photometric matcher. While the scope is limited to two scenes and a lightweight matcher, the negative result is rigorously analyzed through fair paired comparisons and clear oracle bounding.
strengths: Rigorous experimental control: all scoring variants share identical reference views, candidate camera poses, calibrated geometry, and evaluator parameters.
Methodologically sound inclusion of a hindsight oracle baseline, effectively demonstrating that the target gain was impossible given the candidate headroom.
Internal numerical consistency is exact across all reported counts, percentage differences, and absolute errors.
Clear specification of hardware, runtime, software versions, and step-by-step reproduction commands.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to only two scans (SampleSet 1 and 6) and 12 camera triplets, limiting generalizability across diverse surface textures and geometries.
The baseline depth estimator is restricted to a simple 3x3 ZNCC patch matcher across 96 inverse-depth hypotheses, without testing modern learned or multi-scale stereo matchers.
The benchmark lacks statistical significance tests (e.g., bootstrap confidence intervals) across the 12 sampled viewpoint triplets.
suggestions: Expand evaluation across a broader subset of the 80 DTU scenes to determine whether higher selection headroom exists in more complex or anisotropic scenes.
Evaluate whether modern neural stereo matchers (e.g., RAFT-Stereo or MVSNet variants) alter the selection headroom compared to local ZNCC patch matching.
Report per-viewpoint variance and confidence intervals rather than only aggregate count sums over the 6,144 evaluated points.

claims.text: The pilot uses official DTU SampleSet scans 1 and 6, the neutral-light exposure, and twelve reference images on the common robot trajectory.
An oracle choosing after seeing both outcomes could add only 1.27 and 0.37 points over the best fixed direction.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: (928 - 850) / 6144 = +1.27% for Scan 1; (1152 - 1129) / 6144 = +0.37% for Scan 6 from Table 1 data

claims.text: The stronger fixed-direction accuracy at 10 mm was 13.83% and 18.38%.

Choosing the second camera from patch repetition changed 10 mm depth accuracy by +0.08 and −2.54 percentage points versus the strongest fixed direction or structure-tensor control in the two DTU scenes.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Large Scale Multi-view Stereopsis Evaluation
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies the DTU dataset and structured light reference scans specifically to benchmark passive single-photo camera selection heuristics and quantify selection headroom against an oracle.
